skeleton_prune3d — 3D medial op

• Data kinds: voxel → voxel

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.skeleton_prune3d(vol, length=1) (to call the implementation directly, import medial; medial.skeleton_prune3d(vol, length=1); from the registry, ops3d.get("skeleton_prune3d"))

Usage

Prune the whiskers (short branches) of a 3-D skeleton. Endpoint removal repeated length times = branches of length <= length are removed.

3D version of the 2D pruning. Isolated voxels are treated as endpoints and disappear.

Procedure: convert to bool with _ensure_skeleton (if there is an interior voxel, thin with skeletonize_vol), then repeat the following length times: remove all voxels with 26-neighbourhood degree <= 1 (endpoints and isolated points) simultaneously. It stops early when the skeleton becomes empty or has no endpoints left (when only closed loops remain).

Arguments: length is converted with int(length) and clamped to 0 if negative (with 0 the thinned skeleton is returned as-is). 1 iteration removes the 1 tip voxel of every branch, so branches (spurs) of length <= length voxels disappear down to their root.

Returns: a bool array of the same shape as the input.

Caveats (behaviour to know about):

• Long branches also become length voxels shorter from their tips (this is not a process that selectively removes only spurs). If you need the endpoint positions of main branches, the endpoints after pruning lie length inside the original ones.

• A short branch between 2 branch points does not disappear, because both its ends are branch points (degree >= 3).

• Isolated voxels disappear in the 1st iteration.

• The degree is recounted every iteration, so the cost is proportional to length.

Validation (ValueError): input that is not 3-D, an empty array, or containing NaN/Inf. If thinning is needed and scikit-image is missing, ImportError. Downstream: skeleton_endpoints3d / skeleton_junctions3d / skeleton_branches3d / topology_signature.
